title: OOP 01276131 · Lab 05 · INHERITANCE: one rule, how many places?
note: Every number in this lab was measured, not estimated. The two code variants are generated by a port of the course site's own generator (assets/js/viz.js, VIZ["duplication"]), written to disk, counted with Python 3.12's tokenize module, changed, diffed class by class with ast, and then executed: see measure.py / measure_rule.py in this folder and their output measured.json / measured_rule.json. At 8 subtypes and 6 shared fields: copy-paste is 64 logical lines and 8 edit sites, inheritance is 40 lines and 1 edit site. Adding a field to 7 of the 8 copies raises TypeError: Director.__init__() takes 8 positional arguments but 9 were given. Tightening a shared validating setter in 7 of the 8 copies raises nothing at all — the eighth still stores Boss@KMITL.AC.TH. Assumptions: the 6 shared fields and the subtype names are the chapter's own defaults (chapters/05-inheritance.html); one cabinet is one class and one engraved bar is one line of its __init__; the engraver always misses the last cabinet, standing for the human error the chapter describes. Correction found while measuring: the site's line formula for the inheritance variant (shared + 2 + types × 3) undercounts by one line per subclass — the generated code is 40 lines at 8 subtypes, not 32. Cabinets and engraver are our own design, not a real product.
